outcome: location of extrapelvic endometrial ectopic implants
time from surgery to onset of symptoms
cohort: The study included 22 patients with histologic-proven Abdominal Wall Endometriosis (AWE) from a Gynecology Department of a Portuguese tertiary hospital.
finding: Abdominal Wall Endometriosis (AWE) commonly presents as a painful, palpable abdominal mass, often cyclic and predominantly located at previous surgical sites, with cesarean delivery scars being the most frequent, and is typically managed with surgical resection.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery scar was the most common location for extrapelvic endometrial ectopic implants, accounting for 59.1% of cases (n=13).
